rationale: The study clearly addresses urban water supply and sanitation service provision (C1) and regulatory mechanisms governing private sector participation, customer protection, and basic service-level guarantees (C2 narrow and plain). However, from the abstract's reference to 'a review of five case studies' providing 'an overview of the issues involved and some of the mechanisms available', full-text inspection is needed to determine whether it reports primary empirical case-study evidence or a non-systematic policy overview (C3) and whether household/community service access outcomes are empirically evaluated (C4).
plain_vs_narrow_note: Both narrow and plain Criterion 2 readings are clearly satisfied because the paper directly examines regulatory mechanisms governing private sector participation, market power, and social service-level guarantees in urban water and sanitation; under both readings the record is 'unsure' pending full-text verification of empirical case-study methods (C3) and measured access outcomes (C4).

evidence_quotes.quote: The Regulation of Private Sector Participation in Urban Water Supply and Sanitation: Realising Social and Environmental Objectives in Developing Countries
serve as a guarantor of a level of service provision which is consistent with a basic standard of living.

Through a review of five case studies (Abidjan, Buenos Aires, Cordoba, Mexico City, and Manila), this paper provides an overview of the issues involved and some of the mechanisms available to the authorities responsible for the regulation of the sector.
